claim: Voltage-activated potassium (Kv) channels open to conduct K+ ions in response to membrane depolarization.
source: Voltage-activated potassium (Kv) channels open to conduct K+ ions in response to membrane depolarization, and subsequently enter non-conducting states through distinct mechanisms of inactivation.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about Kv channel function, supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Kv channels subsequently enter non-conducting states through distinct mechanisms of inactivation.
source: Voltage-activated potassium (Kv) channels open to conduct K+ ions in response to membrane depolarization, and subsequently enter non-conducting states through distinct mechanisms of inactivation.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about Kv channel inactivation mechanisms.

claim: X-ray structures of detergent-solubilized Kv channels appear to have captured an open state even though a non-conducting C-type inactivated state would predominate in membranes in the absence of a transmembrane voltage.
source: X-ray structures of detergent-solubilized Kv channels appear to have captured an open state even though a non-conducting C-type inactivated state would predominate in membranes in the absence of a transmembrane voltage.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of X-ray structures with expected functional states in membranes.

claim: Structures for a voltage-activated ion channel in a lipid bilayer environment have not yet been reported prior to this study.
source: However, structures for a voltage-activated ion channel in a lipid bilayer environment have not yet been reported.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field prior to this work.

claim: The structure of the Kv1.2–2.1 paddle chimera channel reconstituted into lipid nanodiscs was determined using single-particle cryo-electron microscopy.
source: Here we report the structure of the Kv1.2–2.1 paddle chimera channel reconstituted into lipid nanodiscs using single-particle cryo-electron microscopy.
evidence: This is the primary experimental finding of the manuscript.

claim: The resolution of the cryo-EM structure is ~3 Å for the cytosolic domain.
source: At a resolution of ~3 Å for the cytosolic domain and ~4 Å for the transmembrane domain, the structure determined in nanodiscs is similar to the previously determined X-ray structure.
evidence: This is a direct measurement from the cryo-EM data processing.

claim: The resolution of the cryo-EM structure is ~4 Å for the transmembrane domain.
source: At a resolution of ~3 Å for the cytosolic domain and ~4 Å for the transmembrane domain, the structure determined in nanodiscs is similar to the previously determined X-ray structure.
evidence: This is a direct measurement from the cryo-EM data processing.

claim: The structure determined in nanodiscs is similar to the previously determined X-ray structure.
source: At a resolution of ~3 Å for the cytosolic domain and ~4 Å for the transmembrane domain, the structure determined in nanodiscs is similar to the previously determined X-ray structure.
evidence: This is based on structural comparison between the cryo-EM and X-ray structures.

claim: Large differences in structure between detergent and lipid bilayer environments are unlikely.
source: Our findings show that large differences in structure between detergent and lipid bilayer environments are unlikely, and enable us to propose possible structural mechanisms for C-type inactivation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the similarity between the cryo-EM structure in nanodiscs and the X-ray structure in detergent.

claim: Kv channels are critical for electrical signaling in neurons and endocrine cells, as well as muscle contraction.
source: Voltage-activated potassium (Kv) channels open in response to membrane depolarization to conduct K+ ions, a process that is critical for electrical signaling in neurons and endocrine cells, as well as muscle contraction (Bocksteins, 2016; Jan and Jan, 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Kv channel function, supported by citations.

claim: Kv channels contain voltage-sensing domains that activate with membrane depolarization.
source: Kv channels contain voltage-sensing domains that activate with membrane depolarization, and a central pore domain that opens to conduct K+ ions with high selectivity (Bezanilla, 2008; Swartz, 2008).
evidence: This is established structural and functional knowledge about Kv channels, supported by citations.

claim: Kv channels contain a central pore domain that opens to conduct K+ ions with high selectivity.
source: Kv channels contain voltage-sensing domains that activate with membrane depolarization, and a central pore domain that opens to conduct K+ ions with high selectivity (Bezanilla, 2008; Swartz, 2008).
evidence: This is established structural and functional knowledge about Kv channels, supported by citations.

claim: Most Kv channels enter non-conducting states through distinct mechanisms of inactivation in the continual presence of membrane depolarization.
source: In the continual presence of membrane depolarization, most Kv channels subsequently enter non-conducting states through distinct mechanisms of inactivation (Hoshi et al., 1991; Yellen, 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Kv channel behavior, supported by citations.

claim: The Shaker Kv channel rapidly (msec) enters the N-type inactivated state after opening in response to membrane depolarization.
source: In the Shaker Kv channel, for example, opening of the channel in response to membrane depolarization is only transient because the channel rapidly (msec) enters the N-type inactivated state (Timpe et al., 1988; Zagotta et al., 1990).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Shaker channel inactivation kinetics, supported by citations.

claim: N-type inactivation occurs through a ball-and-chain mechanism wherein the amino-terminal region of the channel plugs the internal pore once it opens.
source: N-type inactivation occurs through a ball-and-chain mechanism wherein the amino-terminal region of the channel plugs the internal pore once it opens in response to membrane depolarization (Demo and Yellen, 1991; Hoshi et al., 1990; Venkataraman et al., 2014; Zagotta et al., 1990; Zhou et al., 2001a2001).
evidence: This is established mechanistic knowledge about N-type inactivation, supported by citations.

claim: Shaker channels lacking the N-terminal region can still inactivate on a slower timescale (sec) through C-type inactivation.
source: However, Shaker channels lacking this N-terminal region can still inactivate on a slower timescale (sec) through a process termed slow or C-type inactivation (Hoshi et al., 1991).
evidence: This is established knowledge about C-type inactivation, supported by citation.

claim: C-type inactivation regulates the availability of functional Kv channels, modulating the firing of action potentials in neurons and cardiac muscle.
source: C-type inactivation regulates the availability of functional Kv channels, modulating the firing of action potentials in neurons and cardiac muscle (Hoshi and Armstrong, 2013; Kurata and Fedida, 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the physiological role of C-type inactivation, supported by citations.

claim: In the hERG Kv channel, rapid entry into the C-type inactivated state underlies the unique inwardly-rectifying properties critical for shaping the cardiac action potential.
source: In the human ether-a-go-go related gene (hERG) Kv channel, rapid entry of the channel into the C-type inactivated state underlies the unique inwardly-rectifying properties of the channel that are critical for shaping the cardiac action potential (Keating and Sanguinetti, 2001; Smith et al., 1996).
evidence: This is established knowledge about hERG channel function, supported by citations.

claim: C-type inactivation in Kv channels is thought to involve a conformational change in the selectivity filter at the external end of the pore.
source: Although C-type inactivation in Kv channels is thought to involve a conformational change in the selectivity filter at the external end of the pore (Armstrong and Hoshi, 2014; Choi et al., 1991; Hoshi and Armstrong, 2013; Hoshi et al., 1991; Kurata and Fedida, 2006; Liu et al., 1996; López-Barneo et al., 1993; Perozo et al., 1993; Yang et al., 1997, 2002; Yellen et al., 1994), its mechanism remains elusive.
evidence: This is a prevailing hypothesis in the field, supported by multiple citations.

claim: The mechanism of C-type inactivation remains elusive.
source: Although C-type inactivation in Kv channels is thought to involve a conformational change in the selectivity filter at the external end of the pore (Armstrong and Hoshi, 2014; Choi et al., 1991; Hoshi and Armstrong, 2013; Hoshi et al., 1991; Kurata and Fedida, 2006; Liu et al., 1996; López-Barneo et al., 1993; Perozo et al., 1993; Yang et al., 1997, 2002; Yellen et al., 1994), its mechanism remains elusive.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: X-ray structures of KcsA mutants that stabilize open and inactivated states have been solved.
source: In the KcsA K+ channel, a K+ selective channel that lacks voltage-sensing domains and whose pore is related to that domain in Kv channels, X-ray structures of mutants that stabilize open and inactivated states have been solved (Cuello et al., 2017, 2010), but the extent to which these inform on the mechanism of slow inactivation in KcsA or Kv channels has been controversial (Devaraneni et al., 2013; Hoshi and Armstrong, 2013; Matulef et al., 2013; Valiyaveetil, 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about published structures, supported by citations.

claim: The extent to which KcsA structures inform on the mechanism of slow inactivation in KcsA or Kv channels has been controversial.
source: In the KcsA K+ channel, a K+ selective channel that lacks voltage-sensing domains and whose pore is related to that domain in Kv channels, X-ray structures of mutants that stabilize open and inactivated states have been solved (Cuello et al., 2017, 2010), but the extent to which these inform on the mechanism of slow inactivation in KcsA or Kv channels has been controversial (Devaraneni et al., 2013; Hoshi and Armstrong, 2013; Matulef et al., 2013; Valiyaveetil, 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about ongoing scientific debate, supported by citations.

claim: The X-ray crystal structure of Kv1.2 and the Kv1.2–2.1 chimera serve as a structural framework for understanding the gating mechanism of Kv channels.
source: The X-ray crystal structure of Kv1.2, a mammalian homolog of the Shaker Kv channel, and those of the Kv1.2–2.1 chimera containing the S3b-S4 paddle motif from Kv2.1 (Kv chimera), serve as a structural framework for understanding the gating mechanism of Kv channels (Long et al., 2005a, 2005b, 2007).
evidence: This is a statement about the importance of these structures, supported by citations.

claim: The 2.4 Å X-ray structure of the detergent solubilized Kv chimera has activated voltage sensors, an open internal pore, and a selectivity filter with K+ ions occupying all four ion binding sites.
source: The 2.4 Å X-ray structure of the detergent solubilized Kv chimera solved in the presence of lipids has activated voltage sensors, an open internal pore, and a selectivity filter with K+ ions occupying all four ion binding sites, suggesting that it represents an open conducting conformation (Long et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a description of the X-ray structure, supported by citation.

claim: The X-ray structure of the Kv chimera is suggested to represent an open conducting conformation.
source: The 2.4 Å X-ray structure of the detergent solubilized Kv chimera solved in the presence of lipids has activated voltage sensors, an open internal pore, and a selectivity filter with K+ ions occupying all four ion binding sites, suggesting that it represents an open conducting conformation (Long et al., 2007).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the X-ray structure, supported by citation.

claim: The presence of an open conducting state in the crystal structure was unanticipated because the Kv chimera C-type inactivates at 0 mV when reconstituted into lipid membranes.
source: The presence of an open conducting state in the crystal structure was unanticipated because the Kv chimera C-type inactivates at 0 mV when reconstituted into lipid membranes (Tao and MacKinnon, 2008) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is based on comparison of the X-ray structure with functional data from lipid bilayer recordings, supported by citation and figure reference.

claim: Lu and colleagues recently solved the X-ray structure of a non-conducting mutant of the Kv chimera.
source: To characterize the non-conducting C-type inactivated state, Lu and colleagues recently solved the X-ray structure of a non-conducting mutant of the Kv chimera (Pau et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about a published structure, supported by citation.

claim: The crystals of the non-conducting mutant contained two molecules in the asymmetric unit, one showing subtle changes to the selectivity filter structure and ion occupancies, while the second was indistinguishable from the open conducting state.
source: Their crystals contained two molecules in the asymmetric unit, one of which showed subtle changes to the structure and ion occupancies of the selectivity filter, while the second was indistinguishable from the Kv chimera open conducting state even though this mutant channel is functionally non-conducting.
evidence: This is a description of findings from a cited study.

claim: The open and inactivated states are either very similar, or the open state is preferentially stabilized by some aspect of the crystal environment.
source: These results suggest that the open and inactivated states are either very similar, or that the open state is preferentially stabilized by some aspect of the crystal environment, such as crystal contacts and/or the detergent and lipid molecules surrounding each channel.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural findings from the cited study.

claim: The gating properties of Kv channels have been shown to be exquisitely sensitive to the lipid composition and mechanical state of the membrane.
source: Indeed, the gating properties of Kv channels have been shown to be exquisitely sensitive to the lipid composition and mechanical state of the membrane (Hite et al., 2014; Milescu et al., 2009, 2007; Ramu et al., 2006; Schmidt et al., 2006; Schmidt and MacKinnon, 2008; Xu et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Kv channel behavior, supported by multiple citations.

claim: Nanodiscs provide a membrane-like environment for membrane proteins.
source: Nanodiscs are hockey-puck shaped lipid bilayers that provide a membrane-like environment for membrane proteins and have been used for structure determination of other membrane proteins using single-particle cryo-EM (Autzen et al., 2018; Chen et al., 2017; Dang et al., 2017; Efremov et al., 2015; Frauenfeld et al., 2011; Gao et al., 2016; Gatsogiannis et al., 2016; Gogol et al., 2013; Guo et al., 2017; Jin et al., 2017; McGoldrick et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge about nanodiscs, supported by multiple citations.

claim: Nanodiscs have been used for structure determination of other membrane proteins using single-particle cryo-EM.
source: Nanodiscs are hockey-puck shaped lipid bilayers that provide a membrane-like environment for membrane proteins and have been used for structure determination of other membrane proteins using single-particle cryo-EM (Autzen et al., 2018; Chen et al., 2017; Dang et al., 2017; Efremov et al., 2015; Frauenfeld et al., 2011; Gao et al., 2016; Gatsogiannis et al., 2016; Gogol et al., 2013; Guo et al., 2017; Jin et al., 2017; McGoldrick et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the use of nanodiscs in cryo-EM, supported by multiple citations.

claim: A typical nanodisc with an embedded membrane protein is composed of a lipid bilayer containing a membrane protein and two membrane scaffold proteins (MSP) that surround the bilayer.
source: A typical nanodisc with an embedded membrane protein is composed of a lipid bilayer containing a membrane protein and two membrane scaffold proteins (MSP) that surround the bilayer (Denisov and Sligar, 2017; Hagn et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge about nanodisc composition, supported by citations.

claim: The success and yield of nanodisc assemblies critically depend on the ratio between MSP and lipids used for membrane protein reconstitution.
source: We first optimized the assembly condition for empty nanodiscs because the success and the yield of nanodisc assemblies critically depend on the ratio between MSP and lipids used for membrane protein reconstitution (Grinkova et al., 2010; Inagaki et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge about nanodisc assembly, supported by citations.

claim: The assembly of empty nanodiscs was optimal at a 1:100 molar ratio of MSP and lipids.
source: Using size-exclusion chromatography to assess nanodisc assembly, we found that the assembly of empty nanodiscs was optimal at a 1:100 molar ratio of MSP and lipids, and that using lower or higher ratios of MSP to lipid resulted in lower yields or formation of large aggregates that elute in the void volume (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from size-exclusion chromatography experiments, shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Using lower or higher ratios of MSP to lipid than 1:100 resulted in lower yields or formation of large aggregates that elute in the void volume.
source: Using size-exclusion chromatography to assess nanodisc assembly, we found that the assembly of empty nanodiscs was optimal at a 1:100 molar ratio of MSP and lipids, and that using lower or higher ratios of MSP to lipid resulted in lower yields or formation of large aggregates that elute in the void volume (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from size-exclusion chromatography experiments, shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The purified Kv chimera was functional after reconstitution into planar lipid bilayers.
source: We next expressed and purified the α and β subunits of the Kv chimera as previously described (Long et al., 2005a, 2005b, 2007; Parcej and Eckhardt-Strelau, 2003), and found that the purified channel was functional after reconstitution into planar lipid bilayers (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from planar lipid bilayer recordings, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The purified Kv chimera could be reconstituted into nanodiscs using a 1:10:1000 molar ratio of Kv chimera:MSP:lipid.
source: The purified Kv chimera could also be reconstituted into nanodiscs using a 1:10:1000 molar ratio of Kv chimera:MSP:lipid.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from nanodisc reconstitution experiments.

claim: Reconstitution of the Kv chimera at a ratio of 1:10:400 Kv:MSP:lipid increased the yield of nanodiscs containing the channel.
source: Considering that embedding the Kv chimera into nanodiscs would necessarily displace lipid molecules, we tested a lower ratio of lipid to MSP with a fixed ratio of MSP to Kv chimera, and found that reconstitution of the channel at a ratio of 1:10:400 Kv:MSP:lipid increased the yield of nanodiscs containing the Kv chimera (Figure 1B, blue line).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from optimization experiments, shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The sample showed nicely distributed particles with easily recognizable side views of the channel in negative staining electron microscopy.
source: The sample showed nicely distributed particles with easily recognizable side views of the channel harboring a rod-like shape for the transmembrane domain surrounded by a lipid nanodisc, and a cone-shaped cytosolic domain protruding from the nanodisc.
evidence: This is an observation from negative staining EM experiments.

claim: Besides the main species composed of the full complex (α4β4), a small number of complexes missing the β subunits (α4) were identified.
source: Besides the main species composed of the full complex in lipid nanodiscs harboring both α and auxiliary β subunit (α4β4),a small number of complexes missing the β subunits were also identified in the micrographs as well as in individual 2D class averages (α4), indicating some heterogeneity.
evidence: This is an observation from negative staining EM and 2D classification.

claim: The cytosolic domain protruded from the membrane plane at different angles.
source: In addition, the cytosolic domain protruded from the membrane plane at different angles (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B), most likely due to the flexible, long linkers connecting the T1 domain in the cytosol and the transmembrane domain of the four α subunits.
evidence: This is an observation from negative staining EM, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B, with an interpretation about the cause.

claim: An initial map of the entire complex (α4β4) was generated with an average resolution of 3.3 Å.
source: We initially generated a map of the entire complex (α4β4) and obtained an average resolution of the entire map of 3.3 Å.
evidence: This is a result from cryo-EM data processing.

claim: The map exhibited a lower local resolution in the transmembrane domain (resolutions of ~4–7.5 Å).
source: However, the map exhibited a lower local resolution in the transmembrane domain (resolutions of ~4–7.5 Å; Figure 2C), likely stemming from the alignment of particles against the cytosolic domain during 3D classification and 3D refinement, and the variability in relative arrangements of the cytosolic and transmembrane domains.
evidence: This is a result from local resolution analysis, shown in Figure 2C, with an interpretation of the cause.

claim: The lower local resolution in the transmembrane domain likely stems from the alignment of particles against the cytosolic domain during 3D classification and 3D refinement, and the variability in relative arrangements of the cytosolic and transmembrane domains.
source: However, the map exhibited a lower local resolution in the transmembrane domain (resolutions of ~4–7.5 Å; Figure 2C), likely stemming from the alignment of particles against the cytosolic domain during 3D classification and 3D refinement, and the variability in relative arrangements of the cytosolic and transmembrane domains.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the cause of lower resolution in the transmembrane domain.

claim: Particle subtraction followed by additional classifications and 3D refinement on the cytosolic and transmembrane domain independently resulted in maps with higher local resolution.
source: To obtain maps with a higher local resolution, we performed particle subtraction, followed by additional classifications as well as 3D refinement on the cytosolic and transmembrane domain independently (Figure 2D and E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a description of the data processing strategy and its outcome.

claim: The cytosolic domain map showed a resolution of 3 Å with local higher resolution as high as ~2.5 Å.
source: The additional two maps showed higher resolution for each domain (3 Å for the cytosolic domain with local higher resolution as high as ~2.5 Å, and ~4 Å for the transmembrane region with local higher resolution of up to ~3.0 Å), which we used to build models of the Kv channel (Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2; Table 1).
evidence: This is a result from focused refinement and local resolution analysis.

claim: The transmembrane domain map showed a resolution of ~4 Å with local higher resolution of up to ~3.0 Å.
source: The additional two maps showed higher resolution for each domain (3 Å for the cytosolic domain with local higher resolution as high as ~2.5 Å, and ~4 Å for the transmembrane region with local higher resolution of up to ~3.0 Å), which we used to build models of the Kv channel (Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2; Table 1).
evidence: This is a result from focused refinement and local resolution analysis.

claim: Three models for the Kv chimera were built: one for the cytosolic domain, another for the transmembrane domain, and a third hybrid model that combines the two models.
source: We built three models for the Kv chimera: one for the cytosolic domain, another for the transmembrane domain, and a third hybrid model that combines the two models which fits in the overall 3.3 Å resolution map of the entire complex (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a description of the model building strategy.

claim: For the higher resolution cytosolic domains, cryo-EM densities for most of the side chains were clearly visible.
source: For the higher resolution cytosolic domains, cryo-EM densities for most of the side chains were clearly visible (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), we could resolve density from the NADP+ cofactor bound to the β subunit (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G) and densities for bound water molecules in areas where local resolution was better than 2.8 Å (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–F).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM density maps, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Density from the NADP+ cofactor bound to the β subunit could be resolved.
source: For the higher resolution cytosolic domains, cryo-EM densities for most of the side chains were clearly visible (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), we could resolve density from the NADP+ cofactor bound to the β subunit (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G) and densities for bound water molecules in areas where local resolution was better than 2.8 Å (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–F).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM density maps, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Densities for bound water molecules could be resolved in areas where local resolution was better than 2.8 Å.
source: For the higher resolution cytosolic domains, cryo-EM densities for most of the side chains were clearly visible (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), we could resolve density from the NADP+ cofactor bound to the β subunit (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G) and densities for bound water molecules in areas where local resolution was better than 2.8 Å (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–F).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM density maps, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–F.

claim: Comparison of the cryo-EM structure in nanodiscs and the X-ray crystal structure in detergent shows that they are similar.
source: Comparison of the cryo-EM structure in nanodiscs and the X-ray crystal structure in detergent shows that they are similar (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a result from structural comparison, shown in Figure 3C.

claim: There is a slight shift/rotation of the cytosolic region of the α subunit and β subunit with respect to the transmembrane domain of the α subunit when compared to the crystal structure, with the most pronounced changes in the β subunit.
source: We do see a slight shift/rotation of the cytosolic region of the α subunit and β subunit with respect to the transmembrane domain of the α subunit when compared to the crystal structure, with the most pronounced changes in the β subunit (Figure 3A,C,D), likely reflecting the lack of contacts between molecules that are present in the crystal of the Kv chimera (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an observation from structural comparison, shown in Figure 3A,C,D, with an interpretation of the cause.

claim: The shift/rotation of the cytosolic region likely reflects the lack of contacts between molecules that are present in the crystal of the Kv chimera.
source: We do see a slight shift/rotation of the cytosolic region of the α subunit and β subunit with respect to the transmembrane domain of the α subunit when compared to the crystal structure, with the most pronounced changes in the β subunit (Figure 3A,C,D), likely reflecting the lack of contacts between molecules that are present in the crystal of the Kv chimera (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural differences, with reference to crystal packing shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Cryo-EM densities for all transmembrane helices (S1-S6) were observed with densities visible for many of the bulky side chains.
source: Although the transmembrane domain exhibits overall lower resolution than the cytosolic domain (Figure 2), we see cryo-EM densities for all transmembrane helices (S1-S6) with densities visible for many of the bulky side chains (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), which enabled us to refine a model for the entire complex.
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM density maps, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: The central pore domain shows higher local resolutions (3–4 Å) compared to the peripheral voltage-sensing domains (resolutions of ~4–6 Å).
source: In addition, the central pore domain shows higher local resolutions (3–4 Å) compared to the peripheral voltage-sensing domains (resolutions of ~4–6 Å), with the lowest resolution for the peripheral loops in the latter domain (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a result from local resolution analysis, shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Within the pore domain, densities for most side chains were observed.
source: Within the pore domain, we observed densities for most side chains (Figure 3—figure supplement 3, Figure 4), providing confidence in the structural model.
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM density maps, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3 and Figure 4.

claim: The transmembrane domain only shows minimal structural differences when compared to the crystal structure.
source: Overall, the transmembrane domain only shows minimal structural differences when compared to the crystal structure (Figures 3 and 4), suggesting that the X-ray structure is representative of the structure of the protein in a membrane environment.
evidence: This is a result from structural comparison, shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: The X-ray structure is representative of the structure of the protein in a membrane environment.
source: Overall, the transmembrane domain only shows minimal structural differences when compared to the crystal structure (Figures 3 and 4), suggesting that the X-ray structure is representative of the structure of the protein in a membrane environment.
evidence: This is an inference based on the minimal structural differences observed between the cryo-EM and X-ray structures.

claim: No discernable structural differences were observed between the cryo-EM and X-ray structures at the intracellular end of the pore where the activation gate resides.
source: For the intracellular end of the pore where the activation gate resides (del Camino and Yellen, 2001; Holmgren et al., 1998, Holmgren et al., 1997; Webster et al., 2004), we observed no discernable structural differences between the cryo-EM and X-ray structures (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a result from structural comparison, shown in Figure 3.

claim: The S4-S5 linker is very similar between cryo-EM and X-ray structures.
source: The S4-S5 linker that is critical for coupling the voltage-sensing and pore domains is also very similar between cryo-EM and X-ray structures (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a result from structural comparison, shown in Figure 3.

claim: No evidence for significant constriction or dilation of the pore was observed in the external pore region.
source: Within the external pore region that has been implicated in C-type inactivation (Armstrong and Hoshi, 2014; Choi et al., 1991; Hoshi and Armstrong, 2013; Hoshi et al., 1991; Liu et al., 1996; López-Barneo et al., 1993; Yang et al., 1997; Yellen et al., 1994), we see no evidence for significant constriction or dilation of the pore (Figure 4, Figure 5, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from structural analysis, shown in Figure 4, Figure 5, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The cryo-EM structure in a membrane environment implies that the protein adopts an essentially native structure in detergent in the presence of lipids.
source: Although the highest resolution X-ray structure of the Kv chimera is at 2.4 Å resolution (Long et al., 2007), and our cryo-EM structure is at a resolution of ~3 Å in the cytosolic domain and ~4 Å in the transmembrane domain, our structure in a membrane environment implies that the protein adopts an essentially native structure in detergent in the presence of lipids.
evidence: This is an inference based on the similarity between the cryo-EM and X-ray structures.

claim: Only subtle structural changes were detected in the external pore in the selectivity filter of the Kv chimera.
source: We detected only subtle structural changes in the external pore in the selectivity filter of the Kv chimera, as well as a small rotation of the cytosolic region of the α subunit and the β subunit, a region involved in crystal packing in the X-ray structure.
evidence: This is a result from structural comparison.

claim: A small rotation of the cytosolic region of the α subunit and the β subunit was detected, a region involved in crystal packing in the X-ray structure.
source: We detected only subtle structural changes in the external pore in the selectivity filter of the Kv chimera, as well as a small rotation of the cytosolic region of the α subunit and the β subunit, a region involved in crystal packing in the X-ray structure.
evidence: This is a result from structural comparison.

claim: Increasing the external concentration of K+ ions slows C-type inactivation in the Shaker Kv channel.
source: Pioneering studies on the Shaker Kv channel point to a critical role of the external pore; increasing the external concentration of K+ ions and externally applied tetraethylammonium (TEA) slow C-type inactivation, and mutants in the external pore have profound effects on the kinetics of C-type inactivation (Armstrong and Hoshi, 2014; Choi et al., 1991; Hoshi and Armstrong, 2013; Hoshi et al., 1991; Kurata and Fedida, 2006; Liu et al., 1996; López-Barneo et al., 1993; Perozo et al., 1993; Yang et al., 1997, 2002; Yellen et al., 1994).
evidence: This is established knowledge about C-type inactivation, supported by citations.

claim: Externally applied tetraethylammonium (TEA) slows C-type inactivation in the Shaker Kv channel.
source: Pioneering studies on the Shaker Kv channel point to a critical role of the external pore; increasing the external concentration of K+ ions and externally applied tetraethylammonium (TEA) slow C-type inactivation, and mutants in the external pore have profound effects on the kinetics of C-type inactivation (Armstrong and Hoshi, 2014; Choi et al., 1991; Hoshi and Armstrong, 2013; Hoshi et al., 1991; Kurata and Fedida, 2006; Liu et al., 1996; López-Barneo et al., 1993; Perozo et al., 1993; Yang et al., 1997, 2002; Yellen et al., 1994).
evidence: This is established knowledge about C-type inactivation, supported by citations.

claim: Mutants in the external pore have profound effects on the kinetics of C-type inactivation.
source: Pioneering studies on the Shaker Kv channel point to a critical role of the external pore; increasing the external concentration of K+ ions and externally applied tetraethylammonium (TEA) slow C-type inactivation, and mutants in the external pore have profound effects on the kinetics of C-type inactivation (Armstrong and Hoshi, 2014; Choi et al., 1991; Hoshi and Armstrong, 2013; Hoshi et al., 1991; Kurata and Fedida, 2006; Liu et al., 1996; López-Barneo et al., 1993; Perozo et al., 1993; Yang et al., 1997, 2002; Yellen et al., 1994).
evidence: This is established knowledge about C-type inactivation, supported by citations.

claim: The T449C mutation in the external pore creates a stable Cd2+ bridge between subunits that favors the C-type inactivated state.
source: In addition, the T449C mutation in the external pore creates a stable Cd2+ bridge between subunits that favors the C-type inactivated state (Yellen et al., 1994), leading to the proposal that the selectivity filter constricts during C-type inactivation (Choi et al., 1991; Yellen et al., 1994).
evidence: This is established knowledge about C-type inactivation, supported by citations.

claim: It has been proposed that the selectivity filter constricts during C-type inactivation.
source: In addition, the T449C mutation in the external pore creates a stable Cd2+ bridge between subunits that favors the C-type inactivated state (Yellen et al., 1994), leading to the proposal that the selectivity filter constricts during C-type inactivation (Choi et al., 1991; Yellen et al., 1994).
evidence: This is a hypothesis in the field, supported by citations.

claim: It has been proposed that the external pore dilates during C-type inactivation based on the finding that C-type inactivated Kv channels can conduct Na+ and larger cations when K+ is removed.
source: It has also been proposed that the external pore dilates during C-type inactivation based on the finding that C-type inactivated Kv channels can conduct Na+ and larger cations when K+ is removed (Hoshi and Armstrong, 2013; Korn and Ikeda, 1995; Loboda et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a hypothesis in the field, supported by citations.

claim: The cryo-EM structure of the Kv chimera in nanodiscs suggests that the structural changes during C-type inactivation are likely not large, and would be compatible with very small movements on the scale <2 Å.
source: Our cryo-EM structure of the Kv chimera in nanodiscs suggests that the structural changes during C-type inactivation are likely not large, and would be compatible with very small movements on the scale <2 Å.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural findings.

claim: It remains possible that the findings are compatible with earlier suggestions that inactivation involves the breakage of a critical hydrogen bond between D375 in the P-loop and W362 in the pore helix.
source: Although the resolution of our cryo-EM structure limits the extent to which we could unambiguously identify the structural changes that occur with C-type inactivation, it remains possible that our findings are compatible with earlier suggestions that inactivation involves the breakage of a critical hydrogen bond between D375 in the P-loop and W362 in the pore helix.
evidence: This is speculation based on the structural findings and prior hypotheses.

claim: Hydrogen bonding between D447 and W434 in the Shaker Kv channel (D375 and W362 in Kv chimera, respectively) has been shown to prevent C-type inactivation.
source: The functional evidence for a critical role of this hydrogen bond in stabilizing a conducting state of the filter includes both gain- and loss-of-function experiments employing conventional and unnatural amino acid mutagenesis (Pless et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the role of this hydrogen bond, supported by citation.

claim: Mutation of D447 and W434 profoundly speeds C-type inactivation in the Shaker Kv channel.
source: Mutation of these residues profoundly speeds C-type inactivation in the Shaker Kv channel, strengthening the bond by incorporating fluorinated Trp slows C-type inactivation and weakening the bond by incorporating 2-amino-3-indol-1-yl-propionic acid speeds inactivation (Lueck et al., 2016; Perozo et al., 1993; Pless et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the effects of mutations, supported by citations.

claim: Strengthening the bond between D447 and W434 by incorporating fluorinated Trp slows C-type inactivation.
source: Mutation of these residues profoundly speeds C-type inactivation in the Shaker Kv channel, strengthening the bond by incorporating fluorinated Trp slows C-type inactivation and weakening the bond by incorporating 2-amino-3-indol-1-yl-propionic acid speeds inactivation (Lueck et al., 2016; Perozo et al., 1993; Pless et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the effects of unnatural amino acid substitutions, supported by citations.

claim: Weakening the bond between D447 and W434 by incorporating 2-amino-3-indol-1-yl-propionic acid speeds inactivation.
source: Mutation of these residues profoundly speeds C-type inactivation in the Shaker Kv channel, strengthening the bond by incorporating fluorinated Trp slows C-type inactivation and weakening the bond by incorporating 2-amino-3-indol-1-yl-propionic acid speeds inactivation (Lueck et al., 2016; Perozo et al., 1993; Pless et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the effects of unnatural amino acid substitutions, supported by citations.

claim: Mutation of W366 in the Kv1.2 channel speeds C-type inactivation.
source: Mutation of W366 in the Kv1.2 channel, the equivalent of W434 in Shaker, also speed C-type inactivation, albeit more modestly compared to Shaker, and both external K+ and TEA slow C-type inactivation in Kv1.2 (Cordero-Morales et al., 2011; Ishida, 2014), suggesting that the mechanisms of inactivation are similar between these Kv channels.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Kv1.2 inactivation, supported by citations.

claim: Both external K+ and TEA slow C-type inactivation in Kv1.2.
source: Mutation of W366 in the Kv1.2 channel, the equivalent of W434 in Shaker, also speed C-type inactivation, albeit more modestly compared to Shaker, and both external K+ and TEA slow C-type inactivation in Kv1.2 (Cordero-Morales et al., 2011; Ishida, 2014), suggesting that the mechanisms of inactivation are similar between these Kv channels.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Kv1.2 inactivation, supported by citations.

claim: The mechanisms of inactivation are similar between Shaker and Kv1.2 channels.
source: Mutation of W366 in the Kv1.2 channel, the equivalent of W434 in Shaker, also speed C-type inactivation, albeit more modestly compared to Shaker, and both external K+ and TEA slow C-type inactivation in Kv1.2 (Cordero-Morales et al., 2011; Ishida, 2014), suggesting that the mechanisms of inactivation are similar between these Kv channels.
evidence: This is an inference based on the similarity of functional effects, supported by citations.

claim: Evidence for the hydrogen bond between D375 and W362 is clearly seen in all previous X-ray structures of the Kv chimera and KcsA.
source: Evidence for this hydrogen bond is clearly seen in all previous X-ray structures of the Kv chimera (Banerjee et al., 2013; Long et al., 2007; Pau et al., 2017; Tao et al., 2010) and KcsA (Cuello et al., 2017, 2010; Devaraneni et al., 2013; Matulef et al., 2013; Valiyaveetil, 2017; Valiyaveetil et al., 2006; Zhou et al., 2001b) (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a statement about prior structural data, supported by citations and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The structure determined by cryo-EM is potentially consistent with the presence of H-bonding between D375 and W362.
source: The structure that we have determined by cryo-EM is also potentially consistent with the presence of H-bonding between D375 and W362 (Figure 4C), similar to that reported in the X-ray structure.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the cryo-EM structure, shown in Figure 4C.

claim: It is possible that the Asp residue can adopt multiple rotameric positions, and that the loss of H-bonding interaction may account for the mechanism of inactivation.
source: However, it is also possible that the Asp residue can adopt multiple rotameric positions, and that the loss of this H-bonding interaction may well account for the mechanism of inactivation, as proposed previously (Pless et al., 2013).
evidence: This is speculation based on the structural findings and prior hypotheses.

claim: Sidechain density for D375 is weak compared to other nearby residues, including W362, Y373, M376 and V377.
source: In our structure of the Kv chimera, sidechain density for D375 (equivalent to D447 in Shaker) is weak compared to other nearby residues, including W362, Y373, M376 and V377 (Figure 4A,C), raising the possibility that the critical hydrogen bond between D375 in the P-loop and W362 in the pore helix may be broken (Figure 4A,C).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM density maps, shown in Figure 4A,C.

claim: The weak sidechain density for D375 raises the possibility that the critical hydrogen bond between D375 and W362 may be broken.
source: In our structure of the Kv chimera, sidechain density for D375 (equivalent to D447 in Shaker) is weak compared to other nearby residues, including W362, Y373, M376 and V377 (Figure 4A,C), raising the possibility that the critical hydrogen bond between D375 in the P-loop and W362 in the pore helix may be broken (Figure 4A,C).
evidence: This is speculation based on the weak density observed in the cryo-EM maps.

claim: Substoichiometric ion occupancy of the selectivity filter was found in the cryo-EM maps.
source: A second piece of evidence that the Kv chimera may be C-type inactivated is that we find substoichiometric ion occupancy of the selectivity filter in our maps.
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM density maps.

claim: Processing different subsets of the data resulted in density maps where ion densities were absent in different positions.
source: We observed that processing different subsets of the data, containing different constellations of particles resulted in density maps where ion densities were absent in different positions (Figure 5A,B,D).
evidence: This is an observation from data processing, shown in Figure 5A,B,D.

claim: In the final refined map, the ion density is absent in the S2 position.
source: In the final refined map, which is the one with the highest resolution in the transmembrane region, the ion density is absent in the S2 position (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is an observation from the final cryo-EM map, shown in Figure 5A.

claim: In the X-ray structure, all four ion sites exhibit comparable occupancy.
source: In contrast, in the X-ray structure, all four ion sites exhibit comparable occupancy (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is an observation from the X-ray structure, shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Ion interactions with the selectivity filter are likely perturbed for the Kv chimera in a lipid bilayer environment as compared to the environment of the crystal lattice.
source: Nevertheless, our results suggest that ion interactions with the selectivity filter are likely perturbed for the Kv chimera in a lipid bilayer environment as compared to the environment of the crystal lattice.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differences in ion occupancy between the cryo-EM and X-ray structures.

claim: A recent X-ray structure of a non-conducting mutant of the Kv chimera reported changes in occupancy of the S1 site in the filter without disruption of the hydrogen bond networks.
source: A recent X-ray structure of a non-conducting mutant of the Kv chimera reported changes in occupancy of the S1 site in the filter without disruption of the hydrogen bond networks discussed above (Pau et al., 2017), suggesting that there may be multiple structural mechanisms of slow inactivation in the Kv chimera.
evidence: This is a statement about a published structure, supported by citation.

claim: There may be multiple structural mechanisms of slow inactivation in the Kv chimera.
source: A recent X-ray structure of a non-conducting mutant of the Kv chimera reported changes in occupancy of the S1 site in the filter without disruption of the hydrogen bond networks discussed above (Pau et al., 2017), suggesting that there may be multiple structural mechanisms of slow inactivation in the Kv chimera.
evidence: This is speculation based on the findings from a cited study.

claim: Recent structures of the hERG Kv channel have raised the possibility of small structural changes underlying inactivation in that channel, including a role for F627.
source: Recent structures of the hERG Kv channel have raised the possibility of small structural changes underlying inactivation in that channel, including a role for F627, a residue equivalent to Y373 in the Kv chimera (Wang and MacKinnon, 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about published structures, supported by citation.

claim: Slow inactivation in KcsA becomes slower as the concentration of external K+ is raised.
source: Slow inactivation in KcsA becomes slower as the concentration of external K+ is raised (Chakrapani et al., 2007), and introduction of Cys at Y82, the equivalent of T449 in the Shaker Kv channel, generates a Cd2+ bridge that favors the inactivated state (Raghuraman et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about KcsA inactivation, supported by citation.

claim: Introduction of Cys at Y82 in KcsA generates a Cd2+ bridge that favors the inactivated state.
source: Slow inactivation in KcsA becomes slower as the concentration of external K+ is raised (Chakrapani et al., 2007), and introduction of Cys at Y82, the equivalent of T449 in the Shaker Kv channel, generates a Cd2+ bridge that favors the inactivated state (Raghuraman et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about KcsA inactivation, supported by citation.

claim: Mutants in the external pore of KcsA either speed (Y82A) or effectively remove (E71A) slow inactivation.
source: In addition, mutants in the external pore of KcsA either speed (Y82A) or effectively remove (E71A) slow inactivation (Cuello et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge about KcsA mutants, supported by citation.

claim: A recent X-ray structure of the Y82A mutant of KcsA suggests that inactivation involves a 2.6 Å constriction at G77 within the selectivity filter, leading to disruption of ion binding sites and water penetration behind the filter.
source: A recent X-ray structure of the rapidly inactivating Y82A mutant of KcsA with the intracellular gate stabilized in the open state suggests that inactivation in this mutant involves a 2.6 Å constriction at G77 within the selectivity filter, leading to disruption of ion binding sites within the filter and water penetration behind the filter (Cuello et al., 2017) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a statement about a published structure, supported by citation and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The D-Ala mutant at the G77 position in KcsA can still slow inactivate even though the mutation would be expected to prevent constriction at this position.
source: Other studies have shown that the D-Ala mutant at the G77 position in KcsA can still slow inactivate even though the mutation would be expected to prevent constriction at this position within the filter (Devaraneni et al., 2013), suggesting that KcsA can inactivate without constriction at G77 within the filter.
evidence: This is established knowledge about KcsA mutants, supported by citation.

claim: KcsA can inactivate without constriction at G77 within the filter.
source: Other studies have shown that the D-Ala mutant at the G77 position in KcsA can still slow inactivate even though the mutation would be expected to prevent constriction at this position within the filter (Devaraneni et al., 2013), suggesting that KcsA can inactivate without constriction at G77 within the filter.
evidence: This is an inference based on the findings from a cited study.

claim: The filter of KcsA can likely undergo multiple types of structural changes that lead to alterations in ion binding to the filter and a decrease in ion conduction.
source: The overall message from these studies is that the filter of KcsA can likely undergo multiple types of structural changes that lead to alterations in ion binding to the filter and a decrease in ion conduction.
evidence: This is an inference based on the collective findings from multiple studies.

claim: The Cα of G372 in the filter fits better in the cryo-EM density without constriction of the filter.
source: In our cryo-EM structure, it appears that the Cα of G372 in the filter fits better in the cryo-EM density without constriction of the filter (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an observation from model fitting to the cryo-EM density, shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The key hydrogen bond between D375 and W362 is preserved in all the KcsA structures that have alterations in ion occupancy of the selectivity filter.
source: It is also interesting that the key hydrogen bond between D375 and W362 that we highlight in the Kv chimera is preserved in all the KcsA structures that have alterations in ion occupancy of the selectivity filter, and mutants of the equivalent Trp in KcsA (W67F) slow rather than speed inactivation (Cordero-Morales et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a statement about published structures and functional data, supported by citation.

claim: Mutants of the equivalent Trp in KcsA (W67F) slow rather than speed inactivation.
source: It is also interesting that the key hydrogen bond between D375 and W362 that we highlight in the Kv chimera is preserved in all the KcsA structures that have alterations in ion occupancy of the selectivity filter, and mutants of the equivalent Trp in KcsA (W67F) slow rather than speed inactivation (Cordero-Morales et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge about KcsA mutants, supported by citation.

claim: The detailed mechanisms of inactivation in the Kv chimera and KcsA may be distinct.
source: Collectively, these results suggest that the detailed mechanisms of inactivation in the Kv chimera and KcsA may be distinct.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differences in structural and functional findings between the Kv chimera and KcsA.

claim: The selectivity filters of the Kv chimera and KcsA can be rendered non-conducting by mechanisms that are distinct for different mutants of the two channels.
source: The results discussed above for both the Kv chimera and KcsA suggest that the selectivity filters of these channels can be rendered non-conducting by mechanisms that are distinct for different mutants of the two channels, and that the detailed structural mechanism may not be generalizable.
evidence: This is an inference based on the collective findings from the Kv chimera and KcsA studies.

claim: The detailed structural mechanism of inactivation may not be generalizable.
source: The results discussed above for both the Kv chimera and KcsA suggest that the selectivity filters of these channels can be rendered non-conducting by mechanisms that are distinct for different mutants of the two channels, and that the detailed structural mechanism may not be generalizable.
evidence: This is an inference based on the collective findings from the Kv chimera and KcsA studies.

claim: It will be important to assess whether higher resolutions can be achieved in the transmembrane domain of the Kv chimera in a membrane environment.
source: It will be important to assess whether higher resolutions can be achieved in the transmembrane domain of the Kv chimera in a membrane environment since these conditions seem to favor the C-type inactivated state without the need for mutations.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: Membrane environment conditions seem to favor the C-type inactivated state without the need for mutations.
source: It will be important to assess whether higher resolutions can be achieved in the transmembrane domain of the Kv chimera in a membrane environment since these conditions seem to favor the C-type inactivated state without the need for mutations.
evidence: This is an inference based on the functional behavior of the Kv chimera in lipid bilayers.

claim: It may be possible to solve structures of voltage-activated ion channels with voltage-sensing domains in a resting state, and with internal pores that are closed.
source: Our results also suggest that it may be possible to solve structures of voltage-activated ion channels with voltage-sensing domains in a resting state, and with internal pores that are closed, to unravel the mechanisms of voltage sensing and voltage-dependent gating.
evidence: This is speculation about future research possibilities based on the success of this study.

claim: The Kv chimera was produced in Pichia pastoris.
source: The Kv chimera was produced in Pichia pastoris as previously described (Long et al., 2007; Parcej and Eckhardt-Strelau, 2003).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods, supported by citations.

claim: Breaking the cells under cryogenic temperature using a ball mill was critical for obtaining tetrameric Kv channels.
source: Breaking the cells under cryogenic temperature using a ball mill was critical for obtaining tetrameric Kv channels.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental methods.

claim: Using fresh Kv chimera (within 1–2 hr from the collection of fractions from size exclusion purification) for nanodisc assembly was critical for reconstitution into nanodisc.
source: Using fresh Kv chimera (within 1–2 hr from the collection of fractions from size exclusion purification) for nanodisc assembly was critical for reconstitution into nanodisc.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental methods.

claim: Compared to regular QF grids, the movement was reduced significantly when using either the 2 nm carbon layer or the gold grids.
source: Compared to the regular QF grids, the movement was reduced significantly when using either the 2 nm carbon layer or the gold grids.
evidence: This is a result from drift analysis of different grid types.

claim: The final pixel size of the map was adjusted to be 0.835 Å based on the best fit of the X-ray coordinates of the cytosolic domain into the 3 Å density map.
source: The final pixel size of the map was adjusted to be 0.835 Å based on the best fit of the X-ray coordinates of the cytosolic domain into the 3 Å density map.
evidence: This is a description of the model fitting procedure.
